questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Cynicism​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Bitterness**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Cynicism"** refers to an inclination to believe that people are motivated purely by self-interest; skepticism. (निंदक भाव)

 
 
• **Example: **His cynicism about politics prevents him from voting.
 
 
 
• **"Bitterness"** refers to sharpness of taste; lack of sweetness. In a metaphorical sense, it means anger and disappointment at being treated unfairly; resentment. (कटुता)
 
 
• **Example: **Her bitterness over the breakup was evident in every conversation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Bitterness**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Conviction** (दृढ़ विश्वास): A firmly held belief or opinion.

 
 
• **Example:** She spoke with conviction about the need for reform.
 
 
 
• **Credence** (विश्वास): Belief in or acceptance of something as true.
 
 
• **Example: **His story gained credence among the villagers.
 
 
 
• **Intuition** (सहज ज्ञान): The ability to understand something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.
 
 
• **Example:** She relied on her intuition to make the decision.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

He must (has change) clothes during the night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **have changed**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of **"has change"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The structure should be in the form of **"must have + past participle"** to indicate a necessity or compulsion that happened in the past.
 
• **"Have changed"** is the correct form to use with **"must"** to express a past necessity or action.
 
• "Has changed" is incorrect because "must" is not followed by "has".
 
• Therefore, "He must have changed clothes during the night" is the correct sentence structure.

Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.

Correct sentence: *He must **have changed** clothes during the night*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Has changed"** would be correct if the sentence were in present perfect tense without "must". For example, "He has changed clothes."
 
• **"Have changes"** is grammatically incorrect because "changes" does not fit with "have" in this context. "Have" should be followed by a past participle when expressing a completed action.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Supplant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Surrender**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Supplant"** means to take the place of (someone or something) by force or treachery; to supersede. (अप्रतिष्ठित करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The new technology will supplant the old methods of processing data.
 
 
 
• **"Surrender"** refers to giving up or yielding to another's power or control; to cease resistance. (समर्पण करना)
 
 
• **Example: **After a long standoff, the rebels decided to surrender to the authorities.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Surrender**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Supersede** (प्रत्यावर्तित करना): To take the place of (a person or thing previously in authority or use); to replace.

 
 
• **Example:** This agreement supersedes all previous contracts.
 
 
 
• **Usurp** (हड़प लेना): To take (a position of power or importance) illegally or by force.
 
 
• **Example: **The prince usurped the throne from his father.
 
 
 
• **Oust** (बेदखल करना): Drive out or expel (someone) from a position or place.
 
 
• **Example:** The rebels managed to oust the dictator from power.

questions.solution:
**The literary device that fits in best here is ‘Oxymoron’, which means ‘****a figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction (e.g. ***faith unfaithful kept him falsely true*** )’.**

The other options,

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The visitor said, "Is your mother at home?"

options.text: The visitor asked me is my mother at home.
The visitor asked to me whether my mother was at home.
The visitor asked to me is my mother at home.
The visitor asked me whether my mother was at home.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The visitor asked me whether my mother was at home.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. We have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• 'Said to' will be changed into 'Asked'. We know that the given sentence is interrogative and we know that in an interrogative sentence 'Said to' is changed into 'Asked'. 
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• We know that the given sentence is interrogative without question word. Therefore, 'If' conjunction will be added. 
 
• We know that 'Your' is changed according to the object of the reporting verb. And it will be changed into 'my'. 
 
• 'is' will be changed into 'was'. 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4. 

 ​

Correct Answer:__ The visitor asked me whether my mother was at home.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Tom pretended not to (heard) a thing.​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Hear'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb form needs to match the structure "pretend not to + base form of the verb" in this sentence context.
 
• "Hear" is the base (infinitive) form of the verb, making it grammatically correct after "not to."
 
• This structure is used to express actions in a more hypothetical or indirect manner, fitting the context of pretending something didn't happen.
 
• Using "hear" correctly reflects an action that Tom is pretending did not occur, aligning with the sentence's intended meaning.
 
• The correction maintains the sentence's clarity and coherence, ensuring the action being pretended (not hearing) is understandable and immediate.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Heard" is the past tense, making it incorrect because the structure requires an infinitive (to + base form).
 
• "Hearing" is a gerund or present participle form, which doesn't fit the structure after "pretend not to."
 
• "Be hearing" attempts to make a continuous aspect, which is unnecessary and grammatically incompatible in this context.
 
• "No improvement" is incorrect because the original "heard" does not fit grammatically after "pretend not to."

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Pinnacle
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Culmination**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Pinnacle"** means the highest point of development or achievement. (सर्वोच्च बिंदु)

 
 
• **Example: **Reaching the summit of Mount Everest is considered the pinnacle of mountain climbing achievements.
 
 
 
• **"Culmination"** refers to the highest or climactic point of something, especially as attained after a long time. (पराकाष्ठा)
 
 
• **Example: **The culmination of years of research led to a groundbreaking discovery in the field of science.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Culmination**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Nadir** (निम्नतम बिंदु): The lowest point in the fortunes of a person or organization.

 
 
• **Example:** The business reached its nadir last year, but has since recovered.
 
 
 
• **Nethermost** (सबसे नीचला): Located at the very bottom; lowest.
 
 
• **Example: **The nethermost regions of the cave had never been explored.
 
 
 
• **Basal** (मूल): Forming or belonging to a bottom layer or base.
 
 
• **Example:** The basal layer of the epidermis is critical for skin regeneration.
